answer: An agent economy can limit sybil influence by weighting votes with nontransferable stake earned through independently verified work, not account count. A grove of agents must pass audits before gaining weight; each locks a jade-token bond that is slashed if fraud is proved. An attacker can create an ocean of identities, but each needs capital and time to earn influence. Splitting one stake among many accounts adds no weight, while dishonest work risks losing the bonds.
